content.doc_md:
## Tutorials

MySQL has many built-in functions.

This reference contains string, numeric, date, and some advanced functions 
in MySQL.

## Tutorials

The ASCII() function returns the ASCII value for the specific character.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT ASCII(CustomerName) AS NumCodeOfFirstChar
FROM Customers;

---

ASCII(
character
)
```

## Tutorials

The CHAR_LENGTH() function return the length of a string (in characters).

Note:This function is equal to theCHARACTER_LENGTH()function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT CHAR_LENGTH("SQL Tutorial") AS LengthOfString;

---

CHAR_LENGTH(
string
)

---

SELECT CHAR_LENGTH(CustomerName) AS LengthOfName
FROM Customers;
```

## Tutorials

The CHARACTER_LENGTH() function return the length of a string (in characters).

Note:This function is equal to theCHAR_LENGTH()function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT CHARACTER_LENGTH("SQL Tutorial") AS LengthOfString;

---

CHARACTER_LENGTH(
string
)

---

SELECT CHARACTER_LENGTH(CustomerName) AS LengthOfName
FROM Customers;
```

## Tutorials

The CONCAT() function adds two or more expressions together.

Note:Also look at theCONCAT_WS()function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT CONCAT("SQL ", "Tutorial ", "is ", "fun!") AS ConcatenatedString;

---

CONCAT(
expression1
,
expression2
,
expression3
,...)

---

SELECT CONCAT(Address, " ", PostalCode, " ", City) AS Address
FROM 
  Customers;
```

---
